question: A post office requires different numbers of full-time employees on different days of the week. The number of full-time employees required on each day is given in Table 4. Monday requires 17 employees,Tuesday requires13, Wednesday requires 15, Thursday requires 19, Friday requires 14, Saturday requires 16,  Sunday requires 11. Union rules state that each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off. For example, an employee who works Monday to Friday must be off on Saturday and Sunday. The post office wants to meet its daily requirements using only fulltime employees. Formulate an LP that the post office can use to minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired. Find the minimal number.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Day index -> required number of full-time employees
    # 0=Mon, 1=Tue, 2=Wed, 3=Thu, 4=Fri, 5=Sat, 6=Sun
    "days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "requirement": {
        0: 17,  # Monday
        1: 13,  # Tuesday
        2: 15,  # Wednesday
        3: 19,  # Thursday
        4: 14,  # Friday
        5: 16,  # Saturday
        6: 11,  # Sunday
    },
    # Number of consecutive working days per employee
    "work_days": 5,
    # Number of consecutive off days per employee
    "off_days": 2,
    "num_days": 7,
}


def _coverage(start_day, day, work_days, num_days):
    """Return 1 if an employee starting on start_day works on `day`, else 0.

    The employee works `work_days` consecutive days beginning at start_day,
    wrapping around the week.
    """
    for k in range(work_days):
        if (start_day + k) % num_days == day:
            return 1
    return 0


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = d["days"]
    num_days = d["num_days"]
    work_days = d["work_days"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets: start days (shift patterns) and days to cover
    model.SHIFTS = pyo.Set(initialize=days, ordered=True)
    model.DAYS = pyo.Set(initialize=days, ordered=True)

    # Coverage parameter a[s, t] = 1 if shift s works on day t
    coverage = {
        (s, t): _coverage(s, t, work_days, num_days)
        for s in days for t in days
    }
    model.a = pyo.Param(model.SHIFTS, model.DAYS,
                        initialize=coverage, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Decision variable: employees whose 5-day block starts on day s
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.SHIFTS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize total number of full-time employees hired
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(model.x[s] for s in model.SHIFTS),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Constraint: each day's staffing must meet or exceed its requirement
    # sum_s a[s,t] * x[s] >= requirement[t]  (>= because text says "requires")
    def daily_requirement_rule(m, t):
        return sum(m.a[s, t] * m.x[s] for s in m.SHIFTS) >= d["requirement"][t]

    model.daily_requirement = pyo.Constraint(
        model.DAYS, rule=daily_requirement_rule
    )

    return model

# Post Office Full-Time Employee LP
#
# Decision variables:
#   x[j] in NonNegativeIntegers, j in SHIFTS = {0,...,6}
#       = number of full-time employees whose 5 consecutive work days START on
#         cyclic day index j (day j, j+1, ..., j+4 mod 7); off days are j+5, j+6.
#
# Objective (minimize):
#   total number of full-time employees hired = sum_j x[j]
#
# Constraints:
#   (1) Daily coverage: for each day i in DAYS,
#         sum_{j : day i is covered by shift starting at j} x[j] >= requirement[i]
#       Source: "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then
#                receive two days off" + the per-day requirement table.
# =============================================================================

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "day_names": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],  # cyclic order
    "requirement": {0: 17, 1: 13, 2: 15, 3: 19, 4: 14, 5: 16, 6: 11},
    "days_per_week": 7,   # horizon length
    "work_days": 5,       # consecutive days each employee works
    "rest_days": 2,       # consecutive days off
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    n = d["days_per_week"]
    work = d["work_days"]
    req = d["requirement"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets: days of the week and the possible shift-start days (same index set)
    model.DAYS = pyo.Set(initialize=list(range(n)))
    model.SHIFTS = pyo.Set(initialize=list(range(n)))

    # Coverage parameter: cover[i, j] = 1 if a shift starting on day j works day i
    def cover_init(m, i, j):
        # shift starting at j works days j, j+1, ..., j+work-1 (mod n)
        return 1 if ((i - j) % n) < work else 0

    model.cover = pyo.Param(model.DAYS, model.SHIFTS,
                            initialize=cover_init, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Requirement parameter
    model.requirement = pyo.Param(model.DAYS,
                                  initialize={i: req[i] for i in range(n)},
                                  within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Decision variable: employees starting their 5-day block on day j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.SHIFTS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize total employees hired
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[j] for j in m.SHIFTS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Constraint (1): daily coverage requirement
    def coverage_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.cover[i, j] * m.x[j] for j in m.SHIFTS) >= m.requirement[i]

    model.coverage = pyo.Constraint(model.DAYS, rule=coverage_rule)

    return model

def build_coverage(data):
    """coverage[(d, s)] = 1 if a worker starting on shift s covers day d."""
    days = data["days"]
    n = data["total_days"]
    work = data["work_days"]
    idx = {d: i for i, d in enumerate(days)}
    cov = {}
    for s_day in days:
        s = idx[s_day]
        for k in range(work):
            d = days[(s + k) % n]
            cov[(d, s_day)] = 1
    for d in days:
        for s_day in days:
            cov.setdefault((d, s_day), 0)
    return cov


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = list(d["days"])
    cov = build_coverage(d)

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.DAYS = pyo.Set(initialize=days, ordered=True)

    # x[s]: number of employees whose 5-day block starts on day s
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.DAYS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.DAYS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # One >= requirement constraint per day
    def demand_rule(m, day):
        return sum(cov[(day, s)] * m.x[s] for s in m.DAYS) >= d["requirement"][day]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.DAYS, rule=demand_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="PostOfficeShiftScheduling")

    day_list = list(d["days"])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Sets
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Set of days of the week
    model.DAYS = pyo.Set(initialize=day_list, ordered=True)
    # Set of possible shift-start days (one shift pattern per start day)
    model.SHIFTS = pyo.Set(initialize=day_list, ordered=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Data-derived coverage indicator:
    # shift starting on day i covers days (i + k) mod 7 for k = 0..work-1
    # These are DATA-derived numeric constants (0/1), not decision vars.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    W = d["work_days_count"]
    n_shifts = d["num_shifts"]

    def covers(shift_start, day):
        offset = (day - shift_start) % n_shifts
        return 1 if 0 <= offset < W else 0

    coverage = {
        (i, j): covers(i, j)
        for i in model.SHIFTS
        for j in model.DAYS
    }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Number of employees hired whose shift starts on day i.
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.SHIFTS,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, None),
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: minimize total full-time employees hired
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.SHIFTS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraints:
    # Each day's staffing requirement must be met by employees working
    # that day. This encodes the 5-consecutive-days / 2-off union rule
    # because shift "i" is exactly the set of 5 consecutive days
    # beginning on day i.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(coverage[i, j] * m.x[i] for i in m.SHIFTS) >= d["requirements"][j]

    model.fulfill_demand = pyo.Constraint(model.DAYS, rule=demand_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATA: every numeric constant in the problem lives here.
# Days are indexed 0..6 = Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun.
# A start pattern s means the employee works days s, s+1, ..., s+4 (mod 7)
# and is off on days s+5, s+6 (mod 7).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA = {
    "days": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
    "req": {
        "Mon": 17,
        "Tue": 13,
        "Wed": 15,
        "Thu": 19,
        "Fri": 14,
        "Sat": 16,
        "Sun": 11,
    },
    "work_block": 5,   # consecutive days worked
    "off_block": 2,    # consecutive days off
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = d["days"]
    req = d["req"]
    work_block = d["work_block"]

    # Coverage: pattern starting on day index s covers days s..s+work_block-1 (mod 7)
    n = len(days)
    coverage = {}
    for di, day in enumerate(days):
        coverage[day] = {}
        for si, start in enumerate(days):
            covered = any((si + k) % n == di for k in range(work_block))
            coverage[day][start] = 1 if covered else 0

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    model.DAYS = pyo.Set(initialize=days, ordered=True)
    model.STARTS = pyo.Set(initialize=days, ordered=True)

    # --- Variables: employees starting their 5-day block on each day ---
    model.workers = pyo.Var(
        model.STARTS,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, None),
    )

    # --- Objective: minimize total full-time employees hired ---
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.workers[s] for s in m.STARTS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Constraints: meet each day's requirement ---
    def req_rule(m, day):
        return sum(
            coverage[day][s] * m.workers[s] for s in m.STARTS
        ) >= req[day]

    model.daily_requirement = pyo.Constraint(model.DAYS, rule=req_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):

    n = d["cycle_length"]
    w = d["work_length"]
    req = d["requirements"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.S = pyo.RangeSet(0, n - 1)   # start day of the 5-day block

    # x[s] = number of employees whose work block starts on day s
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.S, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimise total number of full-time employees hired
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(model.x[s] for s in model.S),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Coverage constraint: on each day, employees at work must meet requirement.
    # Employee starting on s works days s..s+w-1 (mod n), so employee s covers
    # day dd iff (dd - s) mod n in {0,...,w-1}.
    def cover_rule(m, dd):
        return sum(
            m.x[s] for s in m.S
            if (dd - s) % n < w
        ) >= req[days[dd]]
    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.D, rule=cover_rule)

    return model

    n = len(days)
    coverage = {}
